graphEvents.label: Skilled bots identity is the repository, not a person
No actor recorded on approvals answers or run records

label: Skilled bots has no person identity; its identity is the repository owner/name, resolved from pinned job env, then bots/config.json, then env and git origin, with unknown identity refused rather than defaulted.
Everything a run must not write lives in a user-level state root outside every checkout, owner-only 0700, with a pinned state root env that outranks the checkout config.
OpenBot's sign-in is enterprise-shaped: Google, Microsoft or Okta plus runtime SAML and OIDC providers, with one resolver answering both thread ownership and bot-run permission.
OpenBot's administration is a floor plus delegation: INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS is permanent, every role change is audited, SCIM can provision people, and removal deletes sessions and denies the address.
OpenBot's single-user fallback needs OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true, refuses to start when a configured URL resolves publicly, and allows loopback silently or a private address with a warning.
Turnstone's minimal useful shape is admin, operator and viewer roles with granular permissions and allow/deny/ask tool policies; the read-only versus operator split is the part a small team can keep.
OpenGhost uses three per-session permission modes (Ask, Auto, Full access) rather than user roles, expressing posture rather than identity.
OpenMausBot states a local-first, bring-your-own-agent posture with no cloud requirement, matching skilled bots' model and adding no sign-in.

The smallest model for a few people is host-level identity (OS user, SSH key or an --as flag) recorded on definition approvals, needs-you answers and run records, plus one optional read-only viewer and a per-bot name list checked at enqueue and answer time.

Gap: no actor is recorded anywhere today; a definition approval stores only the source kind, an answer stores text and time, and a run record has no requester field, so one actor string on those three records is the smallest fix.

direction: Adding Better Auth or any identity provider
reason: A small team on one host already has an identity in the OS or SSH layer; OpenBot needs an IdP because it serves many organizations over the network.
Owner and admin are the same authority in OpenBot's helper, and a few people need no delegation tree.
They exist to compose custom roles across endpoints; a small team needs one gate, not a policy language.
